papers.title: Machine Learning Framework for Integration of Video and EEG Reveals Distinct Seizure Phenotypes in Mouse Models of Epilepsy.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: The paper introduces an integrated machine learning pipeline that jointly analyzes video and EEG data to classify seizures in mouse models, validated first on a pharmacologically induced generalized seizure model and then on a genetic model of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave discharges. The integrated approach outperformed unimodal EEG- or video-based methods, performed comparably to experienced electrophysiologists, and revealed distinct phenotypes including atypical behavioral and typical non-behavioral spike-wave discharge events.

papers.title: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
papers.summary: The paper defines 'window leakage' in EEG machine learning, where segments from the same participant appear in both training and testing sets, and evaluates its impact across ADHD and Parkinson's cohorts. Using participant-disjoint evaluation, balanced accuracy dropped from 95.59% to 60.98% in ADHD and from 92.02% to 56.17% in Parkinson's, demonstrating that random-window splits inflate performance estimates and that valid generalization requires subject-level separation.

papers.title: Stimulus overlap confounds generalization in EEG foundation-model benchmarks
papers.summary: The study introduces a training-matched audit that varies stimulus overlap while holding test trials, training participants, and stimulus counts fixed, applied across ten tasks from seven EEG emotion datasets. It finds that stimulus overlap inflates differential-entropy decoding accuracy in every task, accounting for 77% of above-chance seen-stimulus performance on FACED-9, and that advantages of EEG foundation models over handcrafted features are concentrated on familiar stimuli, while random controls still show transfer benefits on unseen stimuli.

papers.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
papers.summary: The paper proposes NeuroDETR, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework with structured tokenization and event-aware feature refinement for asynchronous EEG event detection, combining multiscale temporal codebooks and Spatial-Pyramid VQ to encode event-related patterns. Experiments on eight EEG datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance for jointly classifying events and estimating temporal onsets and offsets.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Fatigue Detection from EEG Signals: A Methodological Pilot Framework with Potential for Nursing Applications.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical practice and research
papers.summary: This pilot study used EEG features with machine learning to predict fatigue and found that Random Forest achieved perfect 5-fold cross-validation performance (accuracy=1.00), but performance dropped under subject-independent LOSO validation (accuracy=0.97, macro-F1=0.91), highlighting the need for realistic validation in fatigue detection.

papers.title: Symptoms of anxiety are linked to N3 sleep and lower dissipation of slow-wave activity during nocturnal sleep.
papers.summary: The study examined associations between anxiety and depression symptoms and slow-wave activity dissipation in 70 healthy conscripts undergoing overnight polysomnography. It found that elevated anxiety was linked to weaker SWA dissipation and a greater proportion of N3 sleep, and that anxiety without depression was associated with less REM sleep and elevated alpha power during REM, suggesting impaired SWA dissipation and hyperarousal relate to anxiety.

papers.title: Robust Functional Ward's Linkages With Applications in EEG Data Clustering.
papers.summary: The paper proposes two robust functional Ward-type linkages for hierarchical clustering of grouped functional data, using magnitude-shape outlyingness and modified band depth to select central curves, and demonstrates their robustness and competitive performance in simulations and EEG data analyses.

papers.title: Near-Zero Creep Ionic Elastomer for Non-drifting Ear Electroencephalogram Signal Acquisition.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a molecular design strategy to suppress creep in polymer electrodes for ear EEG by using an intramolecular dihedral structure with electrostatic self-coordination and covalent main-chain bridges, yielding the near-zero creep ionic elastomer Poly(TA-co-TAT)-TAO. The material shows over 200% stretchability, low hysteresis, over 99% recovery, and creep resistance below 0.4% over 12 hours, enabling reliable long-term mental status monitoring with a wearable ear-EEG device.

papers.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study.
papers.summary: This study analyzed resting-state EEG from 20 Alzheimer's disease patients and 20 controls to show that the choice of null model and hub definition in weighted rich-club analysis can produce or eliminate apparent group differences. Using a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs yielded a false-positive rate of 43% under a calibration ensemble, while strength-conditioned nulls with fixed hubs kept the rate near 5%.

papers.title: Paintable In Situ Gelling Bioelectronic Interfaces for Epidermal Electrophysiological Monitoring.
papers.summary: The authors developed a paintable hydrogel that gels in situ on the skin to create a conformal bioelectronic interface for epidermal electrophysiological monitoring. The interface reduced skin-electrode contact impedance to 30 kΩ at 10 Hz (vs. 191 kΩ for commercial paste) and improved SNR from 24.9 to 27.8 dB, enabling gesture recognition (93.4% accuracy) and EEG recordings of α-rhythm and sleep waveforms.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging and electrophysiological signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment with different amyloid-β deposition status: correlations with cognitive function and diagnostic value.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study characterized resting-state EEG and structural MRI signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) with different amyloid-β status and developed a multimodal classification model. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume emerged as promising biomarkers, with the combined model achieving an AUC of 0.852 for differentiating Aβ-positive aMCI, while correlations with cognitive function and Aβ burden were observed.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.summary: This EEG study introduced a frustration induction in the Effort-Doors task to examine frustrative nonreward (FNR) effects on effort expenditure and midfrontal theta (MFθ) power in 83 young adults. FNR increased MFθ power and state frustration, and higher state frustration was associated with reduced response vigor during effort execution following unexpected reward loss.

papers.title: In-laboratory polysomnography as the reference standard in sleep research: a bibliometric overview of human studies.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis of 462 publications (2015–2025) characterized in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) research in humans, showing steady publication growth led by the United States and China, with a stable thematic core in sleep monitoring, staging, and apnea, and emerging trends in machine learning, wearables, and brain modeling.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.summary: In 17 emergency physicians and 18 controls, acute cognitive challenge robustly increased frontocentral theta and suppressed alpha, but no significant group differences emerged after correction, suggesting chronic occupational demand does not alter these EEG stress biomarkers for large effects.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine Inhibition of GABA Neurons in the Ventral Tegmental Area Attenuates the Depth of Sedation in Mice.
papers.summary: Using Vgat-Cre mice and multiple techniques (EEG, fiber photometry, calcium imaging, chemogenetics), this study found that dexmedetomidine inhibits VTA GABAergic neurons and increases GABAergic input to them. Chemogenetic activation of these neurons deepened sedation, while inhibition attenuated it, suggesting their role in dexmedetomidine-induced arousable sedation.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.summary: VAD-EmotionNet, a spatial-spectral attention network with Hilbert-Huang transform features and cosine temporal inference correction, achieved competitive performance on DEAP and DREAMER for EEG emotion recognition in 3D valence-arousal-dominance space.

papers.title: Characterization of the Bispectral Index in Healthy Volunteers Receiving Inhalation Anesthetics in Combination With Opioids in a Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized trial with 211 healthy volunteers, BIS50 and BIS95 values were estimated for five anesthetic regimens; the BIS index strongly predicted responsiveness (AUC ≥0.95), and adding opioids to sevoflurane had minimal impact on these thresholds.

papers.title: Differences in neurovascular coupling in patients with major depressive disorder: Evidence from simultaneous resting-state EEG-fNIRS.
papers.summary: Simultaneous resting-state EEG-fNIRS in 206 participants (134 MDD, 72 controls) assessed prefrontal neurovascular coupling (NVC) via consistency and temporal lag between electrophysiological peaks and hemodynamic responses. NVC consistency increased with age but was altered in MDD and decreased with greater illness severity (partial r = -0.336), suggesting NVC as a potential biomarker.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Microstate Dynamics and their Associations with Acclimatization Index and Serum Albumin in Healthy Adults with Chronic High-Altitude Exposure.
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG microstate dynamics between low-altitude and high-altitude healthy adults; high-altitude exposure was associated with increased Microstate A duration and GEV, decreased occurrence, and altered transitions, with serum albumin mediating some associations with acclimatization index.

papers.title: Dynamic EEG network responses to acupuncture stimulation in patients with stroke: a neurophysiological study.
papers.summary: Acupuncture at Jianyu, Quchi, and Waiguan in stroke patients produced frequency-dependent short-term changes in EEG power (delta, theta, alpha) and whole-brain functional connectivity (delta wPLI decrease, alpha increase), without significant network topology changes.

papers.title: Optimized hybrid Transformer-based model for EEG classification: application to wheelchair control.
papers.summary: This study systematically compared simple and hybrid deep learning architectures for EEG-based motor imagery classification and found that a Transformer + CNN hybrid achieved perfect classification accuracy (1.00), flawless AUC (1.000), zero misclassifications, and competitive inference time (1.17 s), supporting its use in real-time brain-computer interface wheelchair control.

papers.title: Short-term subjective and EEG responses following cervical rotatory manipulation are not reproduced by simulated cracking sound: A randomized controlled study.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 54 healthy volunteers, cervical rotatory manipulation (CRM) improved positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction and altered frontal alpha/beta ratio and alpha band connectivity compared to sham manipulations, while simulated cracking sound did not reproduce these effects.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of induced throat vibrations during vocal emotion recognition
papers.summary: Induced throat vibrations biased categorization of morphed fearful-angry vocalizations while ERPs were recorded. Vibrations modulated frontocentral ERPs from ~75 ms, with source reconstruction showing effects in prefrontal, cingulate, parietal, and temporal cortices, supporting an embodied feedback mechanism in vocal emotion processing.

papers.title: Multimodal Evidence for Large-scale Network Imbalance in Etomidate Use Disorder.
papers.summary: Simultaneous EEG-fNIRS in 54 individuals with etomidate use disorder and 46 healthy controls found delta-band network decoupling and reduced frontal hemodynamic connectivity, with weaker primary motor cortex–inferior frontal gyrus connectivity associated with stronger negative reinforcement craving (rho=-0.471). An exploratory random forest model achieved the highest test-set AUC (0.80) for discriminating the groups.

papers.title: Inclusive electroencephalography practices for Black and Muslim participation in a White non-Muslim-majority country: A co-produced tutorial.
papers.summary: A co-produced tutorial addressing barriers to EEG participation for Black people and Muslim women wearing hijabs in White non-Muslim-majority countries. It provides practical approaches from recruitment to data collection via text, photographs, and videos to improve inclusivity and reduce systemic exclusion in EEG research.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.summary: Exploratory secondary analysis of 26 MCI patients from a randomized sham-controlled taVNS trial found that parietal delta-band power changes correlated with cognitive changes after 24 weeks, with taVNS-related MoCA-B improvement positively associated with relative delta-power changes at P1, P2, and P5 (r=0.629–0.652). Correlations did not survive multiple-comparison correction but were consistent across electrodes, supporting parietal delta as a candidate EEG marker.

papers.title: Neurobiological mechanisms and brain network dysfunction in major depressive disorder: an integrative review.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesizes neuroimaging, electrophysiology, genetics, and molecular evidence to characterize major depressive disorder as involving both molecular dysregulation (neuroplasticity, stress pathways, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, neurotransmitters) and large-scale brain network dysfunction, but notes that direct cross-level evidence remains limited.

papers.title: A homozygous GABRA2 variant associated with infantile spasms evolving to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome alters receptor gating.
papers.summary: A homozygous GABRA2 p.A407K variant from a patient with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome evolving to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was functionally characterized. The variant slowed receptor desensitization; knock-in mice showed depolarized resting membrane potential in CA1 pyramidal neurons, prolonged 6 Hz corneal stimulation seizure duration, and increased locomotor activity, supporting functional consequence without full human phenotype reproduction.

papers.title: EEG Correlates of Verbal and Perceptual Reasoning
papers.summary: Quantitative EEG was used to test correlations of individual alpha peak frequency, relative power, and coherence with verbal and perceptual reasoning scores in participants with IQs from low-average to exceptionally gifted. No significant relationships were found, and the small high-IQ-skewed sample precluded definitive conclusions.

papers.title: Controlled deep breathing technique intervention effects on resting EEG, subjective psychological distress, and executive function performance in young adults.
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial with 40 healthy adults found that a 20-minute controlled deep breathing intervention significantly increased resting-state EEG alpha/beta ratios (especially eyes-closed, parietal), reduced psychological distress, and improved executive function, compared to natural breathing controls.

papers.title: Multimodal art intervention for flourishing in lonely university students: psychological and exploratory neurophysiological outcomes.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 60 lonely university students, an eight-week multimodal art intervention produced significant Group×Time improvements in psychological flourishing, positive affect, aesthetic experience, and an alpha-based relaxation EEG index, but not in attention-related EEG indices.

papers.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
papers.summary: A case report of a 57-year-old woman with persistent post-concussion syndrome after a motor vehicle collision whose CT and brain MRI with SWI/DTI were unremarkable, while multimodal functional testing identified abnormalities across eight domains including vestibular, qEEG, pupillary autonomic, postural, oculomotor, cardiac autonomic, olfactory, and cognitive measures. A 10-modality rehabilitation program was followed by Concussion Symptom Checklist scores falling from 92 to 0 by 17 weeks post-injury.

papers.title: Open-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation Versus Closed-Loop Responsive Neurostimulation in Drug-Resistant Bitemporal Epilepsy: A Narrative Review.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
papers.summary: This narrative review compared open-loop deep brain stimulation and closed-loop responsive neurostimulation for drug-resistant bitemporal epilepsy across 39 included studies, reporting median seizure reduction of approximately 60% to 75% with both modalities but limited seizure freedom. It concludes that RNS may be advantageous in focal or asymmetric bitemporal epilepsy and that treatment selection should be individualized.

papers.title: Syndromic Autism in Helsmoortel-Van der Aa Syndrome: From Clinical Suspicion to Genetic Diagnosis.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 10-year-old boy with syndromic autism and intellectual disability who was ultimately diagnosed with Helsmoortel-Van der Aa syndrome via whole-exome sequencing, which identified a pathogenic de novo frameshift variant in ADNP (c.1239_1240del, p.Gln414Valfs*25). The authors emphasize considering a syndromic etiology in ASD with multisystem involvement and pursuing comprehensive genetic testing when first-tier tests are unrevealing.

papers.title: Neurological Assessment Tools and Inflammatory Biomarkers for Predicting Cerebral Palsy in Neonatal HIE.
papers.journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
papers.summary: Evaluated temporal changes in serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and procalcitonin in 35 neonates with moderate-to-severe HIE undergoing therapeutic hypothermia and 20 healthy controls. Biomarker levels decreased significantly after rewarming (all p < 0.001) but did not predict cerebral palsy, whereas HNNE, aEEG, and MRI each showed strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.summary: A multimodal eye-tracking, EEG, and rating study with 120 participants found that AI-generated Chinese ink paintings elicited higher scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional or digital non-AI works, indicating greater attentional exploration; professional and non-professional viewers agreed on expressiveness but differed on cultural authenticity, supporting a dual-pathway framework.

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.summary: EEG spectral analysis revealed atypical brain lateralization in ADHD: higher average power spectral density in the right brain during working states and left brain during resting states, with theta and alpha waves more dominant in left hemisphere across task states and theta prominent frontally.

papers.title: An all-in-one analytical platform for rapid determination of toxic dyes in complex water by SERS and machine learning.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated filtration-adsorption-SERS sensing platform coupled with a 1D-CNN for quantitative detection of malachite green and methylene blue in complex water, achieving detection limits of 10^-9 M for both dyes. The platform yielded high spectral prediction accuracy (R² = 0.982 for MG, 0.992 for MB) and satisfactory recoveries in spiked lake water (96.37% for MG, 98.14% for MB).

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.summary: Reports a 5-year-old boy with possible EBV-associated CNS involvement presenting with fever, headache, dizziness, and nausea, normal brain MRI, and mild CSF pleocytosis. CSF targeted next-generation sequencing detected EBV, EEG showed reversible sharp and sharp-slow wave discharges, and the patient recovered completely after ganciclovir without neurological sequelae at 1-month follow-up.

papers.title: Excitation-contraction coupling plasticity is revealed upon RyR2 depletion in adult mouse ventricular myocytes
papers.summary: Using an adult tamoxifen-inducible RyR2 conditional knockout mouse model, the authors found that RyR2cKO mice survived with <10% residual RyR2 protein and maintained normal cardiac structure and function, with preserved Ca2+ transient amplitude and ECC gain but slower release kinetics and elevated SR load. These findings demonstrate intrinsic excitation-contraction coupling plasticity mediated by high RyR2 channel reserve and CaT autoregulation.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
